metadata.shortDescription: Learn 1-DP through a Forest of Patience jump-quest story.

story.premise: A neon forest jump quest trains coders to count every route up a tower of ledges using one-ledge hops and two-ledge Flash Jumps before the MP runs out.
story.failureText: Replay the ledges and find the repeated work.

quests.title: Quest 1: The last jump
quests.brief: Ranger Wren asks you to count short Forest of Patience routes by looking at the final hop or Flash Jump into the summit.
quests.learningGoal: See the recurrence: ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2).

hints.text: Every route to ledge n ends with one final move. Which two ledges can that move start from?
Routes ending in a 1-hop come from n - 1. Routes ending in a 2-hop come from n - 2.
The ground has one empty route. Ledge 1 has one hop route.

solution.explanation: Every route to ledge n must arrive from n - 1 or n - 2, and those groups do not overlap. Recursive code makes that idea visible, but repeats work.

problem.statement: Given a ledge number n, count how many distinct routes reach ledge n when each move can climb either 1 ledge or 2 ledges.
problem.gamifiedStatement: Ranger Wren points at the summit ledge. Every safe route through the Forest of Patience ends with either a normal hop from n - 1 or a Flash Jump from n - 2. Count both route families.
inputs: n: an integer ledge number where 1 <= n <= 10 for this discovery quest
problem.output: Return the number of distinct routes to ledge n.
guarantees: Every move is exactly 1 or 2 ledges.
The answer fits in a Python integer.

examples.explanation: The route count follows 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 from ledge 0 through ledge 5.

quests.title: Quest 2: The route scroll
quests.brief: The forest is taller now. Fill one route count per ledge instead of recounting the same vines.
quests.learningGoal: Build a bottom-up DP table where each state uses the previous two states.

hints.text: Your list needs n + 1 entries because ledge 0 matters.
ways[0] = 1 and ways[1] = 1 are the base ledges.
For every i >= 2, write ways[i - 1] + ways[i - 2].

solution.explanation: Write the route count for each ledge once. When you reach ledge i, the two needed answers are already below you.

problem.statement: Given n, build a scroll/list where index i stores the number of distinct ways to reach ledge i.
problem.gamifiedStatement: The forest is too tall to recount every vine. Ranger Wren gives you a route scroll: write each ledge count once, then use the last two written counts to fill the next ledge.
inputs: n: an integer ledge number where 1 <= n <= 45
problem.output: Return a list of length n + 1. The value at index i is the number of routes to ledge i.
guarantees: ways[0] is 1 because standing on the ground counts as one empty route.

examples.explanation: Ground has 1 empty route, ledge 1 has 1 route, ledge 2 has 2 routes.
Each new scroll mark is the sum of the previous two marks.

quests.title: Quest 3: Two-slot pouch
quests.brief: Scrolls are heavy. Carry only the two route counts needed for the next ledge.
quests.learningGoal: Compress 1-DP tabulation from O(n) space to O(1) space.
quests.starterCode:
def next_pair(a, b):
    # a = routes to ledge i-2, b = routes to ledge i-1.
    # Return the pouch for ledges i-1 and i.
    pass

hints.text: After stepping up, the old b becomes the lower pouch slot.
The new upper slot is a + b.
Return both values together so you do not overwrite a before using it.

solution.code:
def next_pair(a, b):
    return b, a + b
solution.explanation: The pouch shifts up one ledge: keep b, and create the new count a + b.

problem.statement: Given two consecutive route counts a and b, return the next pair after climbing one more ledge.
problem.gamifiedStatement: The full route scroll is heavy. The two-slot pouch only carries the two counts needed for the next ledge: the lower count a and the upper count b.
inputs: a: routes to the lower previous ledge i - 2
b: routes to the previous ledge i - 1
problem.output: Return a pair/list/tuple representing (b, a + b), the shifted pouch after one climb.
guarantees: a and b are non-negative integers.
a and b represent consecutive Climbing Stairs route counts.
Returning a tuple is accepted because the runner normalizes tuples to JSON arrays.

examples.explanation: The old upper slot becomes the lower slot, and the new upper slot is 1 + 1.
Shift the pouch up one ledge: keep 21, then create 13 + 21 = 34.

boss.title: Boss: Old Bramblehorn
boss.brief: Clear the real Climbing Stairs problem: count all routes up n steps with 1-step or 2-step moves.
boss.learningGoal: Solve Climbing Stairs in O(n) time with a 1-DP recurrence.
boss.signature:
class Solution:
    def climbStairs(self, n: int) -> int

hints.text: Use the same recurrence: ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2).
The full forest has n up to 45, so plain recursion repeats too much work.
Start a, b at the counts for ledge 0 and ledge 1, then shift the pouch upward.

solution.explanation: Start with the base route counts for ledge 0 and ledge 1. Shift the two-slot pouch until b holds the answer for ledge n.

problem.statement: Given n stairs, count how many distinct ways you can reach the top when each move climbs either 1 stair or 2 stairs.
problem.gamifiedStatement: Old Bramblehorn guards the summit gate. To open it, count every legal route through the Forest of Patience without recounting the same ledges again and again.
inputs: n: an integer number of stairs where 1 <= n <= 45
problem.output: Return the number of distinct ways to climb to the top.
guarantees: The answer fits in a signed 32-bit integer for the given range.

examples.explanation: The route counts build as 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, so ledge 5 has 8 routes.

variants.title: Review: Old Bramblehorn rematch
variants.mutation: Repeat the boss with saved forest towers to reinforce the 1-DP recurrence.
